ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal framework is the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, including the customer due diligence, beneficial ownership, enhanced due diligence, politically exposed person, record keeping, and suspicious activity provisions; the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2011; the Companies Act 1993, including company registration, director, shareholder, registered office, and company-record requirements; the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 1996 where applicable; the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; the United Nations Act 1946; the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; and regulations and orders made under the New Zealand sanctions framework. New Zealand does not maintain a general, fully public central UBO register for ordinary New Zealand companies. Beneficial ownership must nevertheless be identified and verified by reporting entities and other regulated counterparties, and ownership and control information must be maintained in company records and made available to competent authorities where legally required. There is no general statutory UBO filing decree imposing a universal 25 percent filing threshold on all New Zealand companies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, controllers, authorized signatories, major counterparties, licensors, licensees, banks, and intermediaries before incorporation and before material payments. Screening must cover United Nations Security Council designations implemented in New Zealand, New Zealand sanctions lists and regulations administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, politically exposed persons and close associates under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, adverse media, insolvency, criminal, corruption, fraud, and tax-evasion indicators. OFAC screening is not generally a direct New Zealand statutory requirement, but it is mandatory as a risk-control measure where a United States nexus, United States person, United States dollar clearing, United States technology, or contractual sanctions undertaking exists. Resolve false positives through documented identity matching, retain search evidence and escalation records, apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions, and prohibit dealings with designated persons unless a legally valid authorization applies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Companies Register, administered by the New Zealand Companies Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A New Zealand company name must be entered in the form accepted by the Companies Office and must not be identical or almost identical to an existing reserved or registered name or otherwise unacceptable under the Companies Act 1993. English is not mandatory for every word, and non-English words and transliterated terms may be used, subject to registry acceptance, misleading-name restrictions, prohibited or restricted terminology, and the availability of the corresponding company name. The registered company name must use the required legal ending, normally Limited or Ltd. The registry does not generally confer trademark rights, and separate trademark clearance should be performed through the Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand and relevant foreign trademark databases.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term implying government endorsement, statutory authority, regulated financial status, charitable status, or a protected public institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit the name reservation application through the Companies Office online service, conduct identical and confusingly similar name searches, and retain the application reference and supporting rationale. A successful reservation generally remains available for 20 working days under the Companies Act 1993 and related registry procedure, so incorporation should be filed within that period. If the name is rejected, obtain the rejection reason, check similarity, misleading-name, restricted-word, and trademark issues, amend the name, and submit a new reservation. There is no general automatic merits appeal that guarantees acceptance of a rejected name reservation. Where the applicant contends that the Registrar applied the law incorrectly, request administrative reconsideration with documentary evidence and, if appropriate, obtain New Zealand legal advice regarding statutory review or judicial review. A separate objection may be available against a registered name under the Companies Act 1993, but it does not replace pre-incorporation clearance or trademark due diligence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand company must maintain a registered office and an address for service in New Zealand and must comply with the Companies Act 1993 record-access and availability requirements. A commercial virtual office may be used for an intellectual property holding and cross-border licensing company if it is a genuine physical location, is authorized for registered-office use, can receive official notices, maintains required company records or provides lawful access to them, and is staffed or accessible in accordance with applicable requirements. A mere post office box, mail drop, accommodation address, or nominee address without genuine access and record-control capability is unsuitable. The company should also maintain a New Zealand resident director or otherwise satisfy the statutory director-residency rule, unless the director qualifies under the Australia-based exception.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: There is no published statutory inspection probability. For a low-headcount intellectual property holding company using a reputable corporate service provider, the estimated unannounced physical-inspection risk is low, approximately 5 to 10 percent annually. The risk may increase to approximately 10 to 25 percent on an enhanced-risk profile involving non-resident owners, complex royalty chains, high-value related-party payments, adverse media, sanctions exposure, tax-residency concerns, inconsistent registered-office records, or a bank or regulator referral. The estimate is a practical risk assessment, not an official government statistic.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 5 (definition of company), 10-16 (incorporation by registration, certificate of incorporation, legal personality), 17-23 (constitution and company name), 24-33 (shares and shareholder rights), 83-89 (directors and officers), 128-129 (registered office), 151-152 (director residency and consent to act), 200-205 (company records); Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (exemptions for non-issuer proprietary companies); Income Tax Act 2007 and Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for post-incorporation revenue registrations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Level 9, 33 Bowen Street, Wellington 6011, New Zealand; electronic portal: New Zealand Companies Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Incorporation of a Company (prescribed by the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994), filed electronically together with Form 2 — Consent to Act as Director for each director.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: New Zealand has no statutory minimum paid-up capital. A limited company may be incorporated with one or more ordinary shares of no par value (Companies Act 1993, ss 24-25). No escrow account or capital deposit is required for a non-banking, non-licensed intellectual-property holding company. The board must record the consideration received for each allotted share in the share register (ss 27, 29-31); unpaid share capital, if any, is enforceable only as a debt of the shareholder and does not affect the Registrar's certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED
Adopted on [date] pursuant to the Companies Act 1993 and the company's constitution.

RESOLVED:
1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. That the allotment of ordinary shares set out in the Application for Incorporation is hereby ratified and confirmed; that the consideration received, whether in cash or property, is recorded in the share register; and that share certificates be sealed and issued.
2. REGISTERED OFFICE. That the registered office and address for service shall be the physical address recorded in the Application for Incorporation, New Zealand, and that any subsequent change be notified to the Registrar of Companies under section 128 of the Companies Act 1993.
3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. That [NAME] be and is hereby appointed sole Director, [NAME] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, and [NAME] be appointed Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, each appointment taking effect immediately, with signed consents to act filed in the company records.
4. BANKING AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AUTHORISATION. That the Directors and the Chief Financial Officer be and are hereby authorised, jointly, to open company bank accounts, negotiate and execute cross-border patent and trademark licensing agreements, set intercompany royalty rates, and file all necessary registrations and returns with the Companies Office and Inland Revenue.
5. DOCUMENTATION. That the Company Secretary is directed to record these minutes, notify the Registrar of the registered office, and issue documents of appointment within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — New Zealand Companies Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a full name availability and similar-name search on the electronic Companies Register. Verify that the proposed name does not contravene sections 19-20 of the Companies Act 1993 (undesirable names, restricted words such as 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance', 'crown', or 'university', and no likelihood of confusion with an existing registered name). Where a restricted word is used, obtain the written authorisation of the relevant sector regulator. Reserve the chosen name under section 21 of the Act; a reservation is valid for 20 working days. The corporate suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' must form part of the registered name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and up to two alternative names
Sector regulator consent letter for restricted words, if applicable
Applicant contact details and name reservation request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar declines the name as confusing, prohibited, or undesirable, the applicant may (i) resubmit with an amended name; (ii) request the Registrar's written reconsideration with submissions demonstrating that the name is not objectionable; or (iii) seek judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. A fresh name reservation may be lodged immediately at no statutory penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Incorporation Application Suite
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicant subscribers and founding directors; document verification performed through the Companies Office electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare statutory Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) and Form 2 (Consent to Act as Director) for each director, together with the company constitution (or elect the statutory default constitution in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993). Complete full legal names, residential addresses, dates of birth, and the share allotment schedule. New Zealand law does not require notarisation or apostille of domestic incorporation documents; however, non-resident directors and shareholders must have identity verified (certified passport copies or online RealMe verification) and the company must maintain at least one director who lives in New Zealand or in an enforcement country (currently including Australia) and who is also a director of a company registered in that enforcement country (section 151). The registered office must be a physical New Zealand address and may not be a post-office box (section 128).
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Application for Incorporation
Form 2 — Consent to Act as Director (one executed form per director)
Company constitution, or election to rely on the statutory default constitution (Schedule 1)
Share register / first allotment schedule
Registered office consent and physical New Zealand address
Certified identity documents for non-resident directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Companies Office will issue a written query notification listing each defective document or missing field. The applicant must upload the corrected version or execute a fresh consent within the stated response period (usually 10-20 working days). Failure to respond causes the application to lapse, but the filing fee may be applied to a resubmission made within three months; no additional penalty is imposed for a first correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Application and Payment of Registrar Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies / Companies Office (MBIE) — New Zealand Companies Register online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Register and select 'Incorporate a Company'. Enter the data from Form 1, attach the executed consents, the constitution (if adopted), and the registered office consent as PDF documents, allocate the shareholding, confirm the applicant declaration, and pay the incorporation fee of NZ$105.91 (inclusive of GST, approximately US$65) by credit card or online banking. The Registrar's automated system performs an immediate name and compliance screen. On acceptance, the company is entered in the Register and the registration is recorded as effective on the date of lodgment or the later date requested by the applicant.
required_dossiers: Completed application data fields extracted from Form 1
Name reservation number (if obtained)
Uploaded PDF copies of Form 2 consents and constitution
Registered office physical address
Payment confirmation of the NZ$105.91 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the application rather than registering it, the accompanying notice will identify the defect under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993. The applicant may rectify the defect and resubmit through the portal without an additional fee if done within the prescribed period; where the refusal asserts substantive non-compliance with the Act or regulations, the applicant may apply for an administrative reconsideration by the Registrar or invoke judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN Allocation, and Establishment of Company Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office (MBIE), as administrator of the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under section 14 of the Companies Act 1993, which is conclusive evidence that the company is incorporated. The New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is allocated automatically. The board must then: (i) establish the members' register, directors' register, and charges register under sections 84-90 and 200-205; (ii) open the minute book and file this First Board Resolution; (iii) confirm the registered office and electronic address for service in the Register; and (iv) minute and execute the issuance of share certificates. This step is completed in the same session as registration, as the statutory registers are deemed to be created at the registered office from the date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by the Registrar)
NZBN registration confirmation
First Board Resolution minutes
Share certificates and members' register
Directors' register and executed Form 2 consents
Charges register (nil initial entry for a clean IP HoldCo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation or NZBN is not generated automatically, contact the Companies Office Contact Centre for manual issuance. Entries in the Register that are factually incorrect may be corrected by filing a 'Rectification of Register' request; contested entries may be rectified by order of the High Court under the rectification provisions of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Revenue, Tax, and Ancillary Registrations with Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) — myIR Business online platform (www.ird.govt.nz); New Zealand Companies Office for annual return maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 10 working days of incorporation (or immediately if trading begins), apply for an IRD number for the company using the myIR Business online application or Form IR 596. Register for GST when total taxable supplies in the next 12 months are expected to exceed NZ$60,000 (compulsory), or voluntarily where the forecast is below that threshold, and select the GST return frequency. Register as an employer for PAYE, KiwiSaver and FBT if employees will be engaged. Because the entity is an intellectual-property licensing HoldCo, the board must apply the royalty withholding rules under the Income Tax Act 2007 (non-resident withholding tax on royalties and the Approved Issuer Levy regime) before paying cross-border royalties to the ultimate foreign IP owner. The standard New Zealand company income tax rate of 28% will apply, with provisional tax instalments as required by the IRD.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Director and shareholder details
Registered office physical address and electronic address for service
Forecast of New Zealand-sourced taxable supplies for GST registration
Company bank account details (for refunds and IRD direct debit)
GST registration information and turnover forecast
PAYE/KiwiSaver employer documents if hiring staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries the application, the company must supply the requested information within 20 working days. Any adverse tax determination or registration decision may be disputed under the disputes regime of the Tax Administration Act 1994 (notice of proposed adjustment, tax conference, and challenge in the Taxation Review Authority or the High Court). If GST registration is declined or backdated incorrectly, a fresh registration can be lodged with a written explanation and supporting evidence of projected taxable turnover.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. No industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over a non-manufacturing, non-asset-holding intellectual-property licensing company operating under ISIC 6420 / NAICS 533110. Should physical premises or a technical laboratory be established in the future, the competent authorities would be the relevant Territorial Authority (district or city council) for building consents under the Building Act 2004, and WorkSafe New Zealand for workplace health and safety jurisdiction under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating permit, industrial licence, or manufacturing authorisation is required for the ownership, registration, renewal, enforcement, and cross-border sub-licensing of patents and trademarks. The company may lawfully commence its licensing activities immediately upon issue of the Certificate of Incorporation. If the company later employs workers, it must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and, only if it undertakes prescribed hazardous industrial activities (none are within the current scope), apply for a high-hazard facility licence from WorkSafe New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Environment (MfE) and the relevant regional or territorial council under the Resource Management Act 1991 (as amended, pending current RMA reform), with the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) exercising jurisdiction for proposals of national significance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 — Exempt / Not Triggered. Administrative office and intellectual-property licensing activities are not listed activities requiring a resource consent or an Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE). No Regional Plan consent classification applies; the activity constitutes a permitted activity under the relevant district and regional plans. No environmental impact assessment report is required for a company that holds and licenses intangible property only.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC), or air discharge standards apply to a pure royalty-holding company because the activity produces no discharge or emissions. If a standard office is occupied, general obligations under the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 apply, including the lawful disposal of electronic waste and prohibition of objectionable odour or smoke. No trade-waste permit is required for ordinary office occupancy, and no water discharge consents are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a virtual registered office or shell IP HoldCo, no civil-defence clearance, fire-safety certificate, or workplace licence is required. If a New Zealand office with personnel is subsequently opened, the following clearances must be obtained from the territorial authority, Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), and WorkSafe New Zealand under the Building Act 2004, the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015: (i) building consent or certificate of acceptance for any fit-out; (ii) compliance schedule and annual building warrant of fitness (BWOF) covering means of escape, fire alarms, emergency lighting, and smoke control; (iii) earthquake-prone building (EPB) compliance notice under the Building (Earthquake-prone Buildings) Amendment Act 2016, where applicable; and (iv) a documented workplace health-and-safety system with a hazard register, worker engagement procedures, first-aid facilities, and, on any notifiable incident, notification to WorkSafe New Zealand within 24 hours.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD; Te Tari Taake) — online portal 'myIR' (ird.govt.nz), integrated with the New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry for entity and tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned NZ Limited Company must first be incorporated with the Registrar of Companies (Companies Office) and obtain an NZBN. The company must then apply to the IRD for an IRD number using the IR596 form (or online via myIR), providing the NZBN, certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director/shareholder details, and a declaration of anticipated New Zealand taxable activity. Where the company will make taxable supplies exceeding NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period, it must simultaneously register for GST (Form IR356). Where it will pay royalties to non-residents, it should register separately for Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) deduction obligations (Form IR67). Non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners must also provide a New Zealand IRD number or a foreign tax identification number for applicable deemed disposition and land/supply rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — New Zealand resident companies are taxed on worldwide income at 28% corporate rate; however, a close-held NZ company (five or fewer owners, all being individuals, eligible trustees, or other look-through companies) may elect pass-through look-through company (LTC) status; a foreign corporate parent is not an eligible LTC owner, so this structure defaults to entity-level taxation. Territorial scope: worldwide income for tax-resident companies; non-resident companies are taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income (including royalties for the use of IP in New Zealand). No tax-exempt zone applies to a standard NZ Limited Company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Look-Through Company (LTC) election under sections HB 1–HB 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007 (available only to close-held companies with eligible owners); Qualifying Company (QC) election (grandfathered and closed to new elections); hybrid and branch mismatch elections under the OECD BEPS-aligned rules (Income Tax Act 2007, sections FH 1–FH 11) to neutralize double non-taxation; active income election for CFC attributable income; optional GST grouping elections and joint GST registration; and specific zero-rating elections for cross-border supplies. There is no US-style 'check-the-box' regime; entity classification is determined by New Zealand tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (a value-added tax; no separate sales or use tax).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD $60,000 of taxable supplies in New Zealand in any 12-month period (GST Act 1985, s 51); non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' (including cross-border intellectual property licensing and digital services) supplied to New Zealand-resident consumers must also register where total supplies exceed NZ$60,000 in 12 months (s 54B); a separate NZ$60,000 threshold applies to physical services performed in New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol framework (NZ e-Invoicing network) coordinated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE). IRD's 'myIR' and Business Transformation systems accept machine-readable GST returns and electronic records; taxpayers must retain sufficient records for audit but no mandatory government pre-clearance API clearance of invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated where the supplier removes the goods from New Zealand within 28 days of the supply (or within 12 months where the goods are exported under a supply-and-install or hire/purchase arrangement). Services (including the supply, granting, or assignment of patents, trademarks, and other intellectual property rights) are zero-rated where supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not supplied in connection with land in New Zealand, goods in New Zealand at the time of supply, or supplied to a non-resident GST-registered person who acquires the services for the purpose of making taxable supplies in New Zealand (and the supplier knows or ought to know that fact). Royalty income from offshore patent sub-licensing is therefore zero-rated where the licensee is a non-resident acting outside New Zealand; the supplier must hold contemporaneous documentation of the licensee's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service 'Trade Single Window') and approved export entry confirmation
Signed license/sub-license agreement and royalty calculation working papers
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other shipping/transport evidence of physical export (for goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/telex credit confirmation evidencing receipt of the foreign-currency royalty payment
Certificate of Tax Residence or equivalent evidence of licensee's non-resident status
Delivery and service performance records evidencing that the IP is exploited offshore
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD and New Zealand Customs may disallow zero-rating and claw back GST (plus use-of-money interest) where goods are not exported within the statutory window or where services are in fact enjoyed or used in New Zealand, or where the supplier failed to obtain sufficient evidence of export or non-residence. Shortfall penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for taking an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion/fraud with a false or misleading GST return. Fraudulent or abusive zero-rating claims are subject to no time-bar and criminal prosecution; bona fide errors are generally time-barred after four years from the end of the relevant return period. Cross-border royalty structures also face transfer-pricing adjustment, non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) recharacterization, and the hybrid mismatch rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), constituted under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 as the prudential regulator and monetary authority; foreign exchange administration is decentralized and the Reserve Bank does not operate exchange-control machinery. The Overseas Investment Office (OIO), operating under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, screens foreign investment in sensitive New Zealand assets, and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervises market conduct, while the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) and the Reserve Bank jointly administer the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 regime for reporting entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both the capital and current accounts. New Zealand maintains no exchange control regulations, no central bank approval requirement for inward or outward remittances, no restrictions on profit repatriation, and no differentiated treatment for capital vs current account transactions. Dividends, royalties, interest, and intercompany loan repayments may be remitted freely from New Zealand, subject only to standard documentary verification by the bank and statutory tax deduction obligations (Non-Resident Withholding Tax on payments to non-residents). The Overseas Investment Act 2005 requires consent for acquisitions of significant business assets (generally NZD 100 million or above), sensitive land, or fishing quota; ordinary global IP patent-licensing royalty flows and standard treasury operations are not notifiable unless an equity or asset acquisition of that magnitude is structured.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline exist in New Zealand. Royalty and licensing receipts earned by a New Zealand entity from global IP patent exploitation may be retained in foreign currency in onshore foreign-currency accounts, converted to NZD at the entity's discretion, or kept offshore with licensed banking partners. The Reserve Bank does not require any reporting or escrow of trade or royalty receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account: ANZ Business 'Call' or 'Term Deposit' ring-fenced for subscribed capital and initial IP-contribution proceeds; Operational Account: ANZ Business Plus transaction account with foreign-currency sub-accounts (USD, EUR, GBP, AUD).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ASB Bank Limited (subsidiary of Commonwealth Bank of Australia)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account: ASB 'Business Saver' segregated deposit; Operational Account: ASB 'Business Direct' with multi-currency wallet and online SWIFT payment module.
Capital Escrow Account: BNZ 'Corporate Call Account'; Operational Account: BNZ 'Business Plus' with BNZ Corporate Online FX, FX forwards, and cross-currency swap lines.
Capital Escrow Account: Westpac 'At Call Corporate Deposit'; Operational Account: Westpac 'Business Banking Account' with integrated Trade Finance and Letter-of-Credit desk.
Capital Escrow Account: Kiwibank 'Business Term Deposit'; Operational Account: Kiwibank 'Business Everyday' account (limited foreign-currency and corporate hedging product depth).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for cross-border payment facilitation, Low for full local clearing replacement. New Zealand does not maintain a standalone Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing category; offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, etc.) operate as non-bank payment service providers and must partner with an RBNZ-registered bank to access local NZD settlement via the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). An offshore EMI may lawfully provide multi-currency collection accounts (virtual IBANs) for inbound royalty receipts and execute onward SWIFT disbursements, but the entity should register on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 if services are offered to New Zealand-based persons. For capital-contribution escrow integrity, audit trail, and final settlement in NZD, a direct Tier-1 domestic bank relationship is strongly preferred; EMIs should be used only as an ancillary liquidity-collection rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or high-assurance identity interview is mandatory for an ISIC 6420 IP-holding company rated Medium-Risk Enhanced under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. New Zealand banks require the physical presence at a New Zealand branch of at least one director or the authorized local agent, or a bank-approved live video-identification session with notarized (and where relevant apostilled) passport, proof-of-residence, corporate extract, and board resolution delivered by secure courier. The Companies Act 1993 further requires the NZ company to maintain a registered office in New Zealand and to have at least one director resident in New Zealand (or in Australia if that director is also a director of an Australian-incorporated company); consequently, fully remote onboarding without any NZ-resident director or NZ-based agent is not permitted. A licensed corporate-services provider can act as authorized agent under a certified power of attorney for the interview, but the ultimate beneficial owner must be identified and the bank's Compliance Officer must ratify the Enhanced Due Diligence file before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership is layered through a foreign trust or multi-tier corporate chain, presenting an opaque ownership picture.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled trust deed or group-structure deed; New Zealand Companies Office certificate of incorporation, share register, and certificate of good standing; a sworn UBO declaration on the bank's template; full group structure diagram identifying all intermediate holding entities; directors' resolution appointing authorized signatories; and certification of good standing from the ultimate parent's registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection derives from offshore IP royalty pools or a parent company in a jurisdiction raising source-of-wealth questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the NZ Ltd and, where available, the ultimate parent (New Zealand IFRS or equivalent) for the prior two to three years; executed patent/trademark license agreements and global sub-license contracts; an independent IP valuation or transfer-pricing benchmarking report aligned with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and New Zealand Inland Revenue transfer-pricing practice; and three months of source-account bank statements preceding the transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-heavy license income triggers Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) because revenue has no physical supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ) register extracts for NZ-registered marks/patents and equivalent foreign register extracts; valid IRD number and NZBN; NZ GST registration certificate if registered; documented board minutes demonstrating New Zealand-based decision-making (IP portfolio management, license negotiations, and accounting substance); and a statutory declaration confirming that the entity has real economic substance in New Zealand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound SWIFT wires contain mismatched purpose codes or narratives such as 'IP sale' or 'consultancy' which contradict the license model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank-registered remittance-narrative protocol mandating the code 'IP ROYALTY – LICENSE AGREEMENT [DATE/REF]' on every inbound transfer; pre-notification compliance package comprising the up-to-date invoice or royalty certificate, the underlying sub-license agreement cover page, and the sanctioned-party/screening clearances (OFAC, UK/HMT, UN, and ASIA lists) obtained by the remitting bank; and an annual compliance undertaking signed by the director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership combined with a bare registered office and no physical presence is assessed as a shell-company risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of substance: lease agreement for New Zealand premises (or contracted serviced-office with dedicated meeting facilities), employment or board-service agreements of the NZ-resident director, minutes of annual general meetings and board meetings physically held in New Zealand, local bookkeeping records, and New Zealand tax filings (income tax, GST, and RWT/NRWT returns) demonstrating ongoing compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and intercompany shareholder loans are routed as SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202/MT202 COV (large-value bank-to-bank transfer) from the parent's or affiliate's bank to the NZ receiving bank's SWIFT BIC. The payment must carry a capital-account purpose code, generally 'EQUI' (Equity Investment) for subscription proceeds or 'INTR'/'LOAN' (Intercompany Loan), accompanied by a strict narrative referencing the board resolution date and the executed subscription or intercompany loan agreement. The bank's verification package requires the certified board resolution of NZ Ltd, an executed share subscription or loan agreement compliant with the Companies Act 1993 sections on financial assistance and capital maintenance, an updated share register, the NZBN and IRD number, and a Source of Funds declaration. Inbound funds are parked in the Capital Escrow Account until full documentary compliance is confirmed, after which they are released to the Operational Account; all clearings finalize through the RBNZ-licensed bank's settlement on the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound royalty settlements and trade disbursements are cleared primarily via SWIFT MT103 across the NZ bank's global correspondent network (typically US Dollar clearance through CHIPS/Fedwire New York and Euro clearance through TARGET2 Frankfurt). Each MT103 must reference the governing license agreement and indicate the Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) treatment; where the payee is a non-resident licensor without a treaty-reduced rate, the bank applies NRWT under the Income Tax Act 2007 and remits it to Inland Revenue, and may accept an IRD 902 certificate from the withholding agent for rate confirmation. For structured trade settlements, an Irrevocable Confirmed Commercial Letter of Credit issued through the bank's trade-finance desk (tenor typically 30 to 180 days) is available, requiring presentation of the commercial invoice, an executed sub-license utilization certificate, and any documentary evidence specified by the underlying licensing agreement; alternative rails include virtual-IBAN facilitation through licensed EMIs for low-value recurring royalties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forwards (NZD versus USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, JPY) up to 36 months under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's master FX trading terms, used for conversion-rate certainty on committed royalty flows.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CIRS) for matched-maturity hedging of intercompany loans and long-dated IP acquisition consideration.
European-style FX Options (vanilla put/call structures) for downside protection on large, one-off lump-sum royalty receipts while preserving upside participation.
FX Swaps and Tom-Next (Overnight) Rollovers for treasury liquidity management across time zones.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted only on an exceptional, documented basis where the counterparty currency is non-deliverable due to sanctions or limited convertibility; NDFs are not used for NZD pairs because the NZD is fully deliverable and freely convertible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993 s 209) — statutory company declaration confirming registered office, directors, shareholders and share structure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date (anniversary of incorporation date, unless otherwise fixed by the constitution).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A fine of up to NZD 10,000 on the company and each director for non-filing (Companies Act 1993 s 374(1)(a)); if annual returns are not filed for more than three consecutive years, the Registrar may give notice and remove the company from the New Zealand Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements (audited where required) — filed as a reporting entity only if the company is large, an issuer, an overseas company, or a member of a reporting group under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the annual meeting at which the financial statements are approved; the annual meeting must be held within 6 months of the company's balance date (Companies Act 1993 s 202 and s 210).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and the company may incur monetary penalties under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for late or non-filing; continued default can support Registrar strike-off action and a director disqualification application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) and International Dealings Schedule (IDS) — disclosing cross-border related-party patent and trademark royalty transactions and transfer-pricing positions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March balance date: IR4 and IDS due by 7 July following the balance date; extended due dates apply to registered tax-agent clients.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return: initial penalty NZD 250 and an additional NZD 250 per month (maximum six months); unpaid terminal tax attracts late payment penalties of 1% per month and Use-of-Money-Interest (UOMI) from the applicable due date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST Return (GST101) — six-monthly taxable-period return where GST-registered; alternative monthly or two-monthly frequencies may be elected by the company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the 28th day of the month following the close of the taxable period (e.g., periods ending 31 March and 30 September are due 28 April and 28 October respectively).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-filing penalty of NZD 50 for the first event and escalating penalties for subsequent events; late-payment penalties (1% per month) and UOMI accrue on unpaid GST.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) return (IR67) on royalty payments remitted to non-resident licensors in the patent licensing chain.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly: due with payment on the 20th day of the month following the month in which the royalty or interest payment was made to the non-resident.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deduction of NRWT makes the company assessable for the unreported tax; late-payment penalties (up to 10% per month for accumulated debt) and UOMI are imposed, with prosecution available for persistent failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company is a reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013: total assets exceed NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeds NZD 30 million in either of the two preceding accounting periods; the company is an FMC reporting entity (issuer); the company is an overseas company; or the shareholders (or the board, if shareholders so resolve) pass a resolution requiring an audit. Non-reporting small/medium IP holding companies are not required to have an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP): Tier 1 entities apply NZ IFRS; Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS RDR (reduced-disclosure regime) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB); non-reporting companies preparing tax-only financial information follow Income Tax Act 2007 record-keeping standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate public UBO (beneficial ownership) annual filing for a non-listed limited company. The Annual Return (filed on the Companies Register) annually re-confirms the registered shareholders and directors. Share transfers are legally effective only when recorded in the company's Register of Members (Companies Act 1993 s 91); the company must notify the Companies Office of shareholding and director changes within 20 working days of the change. Where the company is an AML/CFT obliged entity, customer due-diligence files must identify and annually review ultimate beneficial owners of 25% or more of the shares or voting rights; for a private IP licensing company not carrying on financial services, no UBO return is filed with the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,000 per annum (NZD 800 - NZD 1,650) for a New Zealand registered office, statutory agent and company secretarial service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per annum (NZD 10,000 - NZD 30,000) for an annual certified audit of a small-to-medium IP holding/licensing company where audit is required or voluntarily commissioned

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory corporate tax holidays or patent-box regime exist in New Zealand. Effective tax rate mitigants are: (i) the R&D Tax Credit of 15% of eligible R&D expenditure (Income Tax Act 2007, s DZ 15); (ii) full deductibility of IP acquisition costs and depreciation of depreciable intangible property (s EE); (iii) the imputation credit system, which avoids double taxation of NZ-resident shareholders; and (iv) loss continuity rules permitting utilisation of prior-year losses. Royalty income derived by an IP HoldCo is taxed at the standard 28% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed through Inland Revenue's myIR secure online portal or via IRD-compliant software-to-software e-filing (GST and provisional tax may be administered through the same portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax payments are made three times during the year, with a terminal tax payment at year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July after the balance date; terminal tax is due 7 April after the balance date; provisional tax instalments are due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May. Non-standard balance dates carry a filing deadline of the last day of the fourth month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: gross royalties, license fees, sub-licensing receipts, and all other assessable income derived from the worldwide IP licensing business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Completed by the NZ-resident company for its worldwide income; non-resident shareholders must not include their own receipts on this line and cannot claim treaty exemption from the company's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses: deductible operating costs, legal fees, amortisation of patents, intercompany royalty payments, interest, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only to the extent incurred in deriving assessable income and at arm's length; non-resident related-party payees must be separately reported in transfer pricing disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax: Box 1 less Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is a computation line; non-resident shareholders have no direct entry and any loss utilisation is subject to NZ continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss-offset: current-year losses or prior-year tax losses utilised against taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses can be offset only if shareholder continuity or business continuity tests are satisfied; transfers of shares to non-residents may break continuity.
This line is the base for the 28% corporate tax computation; it does not represent a dividend taxable in the hands of non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax on taxable income at 28%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company is the taxpayer; non-resident shareholders are not assessed on this line and cannot use the company's tax rate as a treaty shield.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends, resident withholding tax credits, and foreign tax credits claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits are generally not refundable to non-resident shareholders; the supplementary dividend mechanism may be used to pass a full treaty-rate outcome.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax payable or refundable: final liability after credits and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any unpaid residual tax is a company debt; directors may become personally liable for unpaid RWT/NRWT-related defaults.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure: declaration whether cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million in aggregate revenue or expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parents must supply the NZ company with TP documentation acceptable to Inland Revenue; the declaration remains the NZ company's statutory obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border payments and NRWT schedule: royalties, interest, and dividends paid to non-residents, including NRWT deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident recipients should hold a New Zealand Certificate of Residence and Form IR290 declaration to enable treaty-reduced rates; the payer must retain these documents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 per IR4 return, escalating to NZD 500 for repeat late returns; late payment penalty of 1% on the day after the due date, an additional 4% after 7 days, and a further 1% per month thereafter. Interest (TAA, s 120) is imposed on unpaid tax; deliberate failure to file is a criminal offence punishable by a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and, for evasion, imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder not carrying on business in New Zealand. Under New Zealand's DTAs the rate is commonly reduced to 15% for portfolio holdings and 5% for substantial corporate shareholdings, and the supplementary dividend regime allows the effective combined corporate plus withholding cost to align with the treaty rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its own tax authority; (2) complete Inland Revenue Form IR290 declaring entitlement to the DTA; and (3) provide both documents to the NZ paying company before distribution. The NZ payer applies the treaty rate from the date the valid declaration is held, retains the TRC and IR290 for audit purposes, and files the appropriate withholding returns; for supplementary dividends, the company attaches imputation credits and files the accompanying supplementary dividend worksheet with the imputation return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic NRWT is 15% on royalties and 15% on interest paid to non-residents. Under New Zealand's tax treaties, royalty rates are frequently reduced to 10% or 5%, and interest rates to 10% or 15%; an interest payment to an unassociated lender may instead bear the Approved Issuer Levy of 2% if the lender is a registered institution. An IP HoldCo paying licence fees to a foreign patent owner must withhold NRWT at 15% absent treaty relief, and must obtain the same IR290/TRC protocol for reduced rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million in aggregate cross-border related-party revenue or expenses triggers mandatory transfer pricing documentation and an explicit IR4 disclosure; OECD-aligned Master File and Local File are expected for MNE groups, and Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory where consolidated group revenue exceeds NZD 1.3 billion (approximately EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no codified Economic Substance Regulations in the UAE/GCC sense. However, the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007, s BG 1), the corporate residence rules (s YD 2), imputation continuity requirements, and the transfer pricing recharacterisation power (s GC 13) require genuine commercial substance, local board control, real IP management functions, and economic activity in New Zealand. An IP HoldCo with no staff, premises, or substantive decision-making is vulnerable to recharacterisation, denial of deductions, and penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly or dishonestly omitting royalty income from the IR4, fabricating licence-related expenses, or submitting false transfer pricing records to Inland Revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall under s 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994; criminal conviction liable to a fine of up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years; unpaid tax, use-of-money interest, and penalties remain collectable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in evasion face joint and several liability for the company's unpaid tax where a corporate sham is established; personal liability for unpaid RWT/NRWT and related penalties under s 149A; Departure Prohibition Orders under s 41C prevent directors from leaving New Zealand; imprisonment of up to 5 years may attach to individual officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Arrangement and GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating NZ_LTD as a bare IP conduit with no employees, premises, or board activity in New Zealand, executing a round-trip patent licence designed solely to shift profits to a connected foreign entity or preferential regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may cancel the tax advantage under s BG 1/s GB 1, reconstruct the arrangement, reallocate income at arm's length under s GC 13, deny foreign tax credits, impose shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% under s 141, and assess interest from the original payment date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors aware of the sham may be personally liable for company tax defaults under s 149A; asset preservation and Departure Prohibition Orders may issue; directors face disqualification under the Companies Act 1993 for fraudulent conduct and personal civil claims for restitution by creditors, including Inland Revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume intercompany royalty wire flows through New Zealand payment rails without customer due diligence, or where directors know the licensing fees represent proceeds of foreign corruption, bribery, or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties under the AML/CFT Act 2009 of up to NZD 2,000,000 per contravention for reporting entities; criminal money laundering liability under s 243 of the Crimes Act 1961 with imprisonment for up to 7 years; asset forfeiture orders may be made.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers and directors may be prosecuted individually; personal fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years may be imposed on individuals involved in laundering; reckless directors can be sued for the financial loss suffered by the company or affected third parties, and banking relationships will be terminated with cross-border blacklisting consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recharacterising dividends to non-resident shareholders as 'royalties', 'management fees', or 'service fees' to avoid the 30% dividend NRWT, or failing to deduct and remit NRWT on the true distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the disguised distribution as a dividend under s GB 1; NRWT assessed at 30% on the recharacterised amount; shortfall penalties for evasion of up to 150%; use-of-money interest; cancellation of imputation credits if the imputation account is in deficit, imposing a further 28% ICA charge on the NZ company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to take reasonable steps to ensure the company deducts and pays NRWT are personally liable under s 149A; Departure Prohibition Orders bar directors from leaving New Zealand until the tax is secured; deliberate non-deduction is a criminal offence carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines; corporate veil-piercing permits recovery against personal assets of directors.
